summary: 1936 CCC-built steel tower in Martin County, NC; a March 2018 state surplus bid notice on its site also places the tower on state-owned land. Sources do not say what happened after.

facts.status_note: A March 22, 2018 state surplus property bid notice appears on the site, which also places the tower on state-owned land. No dated source says whether it sold or what condition it is in now.

events.note: Register build year; a 1938 state report dates completion to September 4, 1936, by CCC Camp P-67
Frame living quarters and garage, 24 x 30 ft, finished at the site in June 1938 by CCC Camp P-67
Site entry: bids opened on state surplus property, March 22, 2018; the same entry places the tower on state-owned land

evidence.supports: near the Roanoke River in eastern NC; state-owned; built 1936
evidence.quote: Located near the Roanoke River in eastern North Carolina, this state-owned tower was built in 1936.

evidence.supports: administered by the North Carolina Forest Service
completed September 4, 1936 by CCC at Camp P-67; steel tower 99 ft 9 in
evidence.quote: September 4, 1936: A 99-foot 9-inch steel tower was completed by members of CCC at Camp P-67.

evidence.supports: source is a 1938 state biennial report
evidence.quote: (Department of Conservation and Development - 7th Biennial Report - 1938)

evidence.supports: June 6, 1938 frame living quarters and garage, 24 x 30 ft, at the site
evidence.quote: June 6, 1938: A three room frame combination living quarters and garage 24 x 30 feet completed at the Hassel tower site.

evidence.supports: the 1938 building work was done by CCC Camp P-67 members
evidence.quote: The work was done by members of the CCC Camp P-67.
March 22, 2018: Auction was opened for bids on state surplus property.
Tower located on state owned land.

corrections.why: The lookout history site gives the tower as 99 feet 9 inches, about 30.4 m. No cited source supports 30.2 m.

notes_for_editor: Build year (1936) and height are supported by two sources. The fate after the March 2018 surplus bid notice is unknown: check the NC state surplus records for an outcome, and ask the NC Forest Service about current status and access. No staffing source found, and no access or visit source, so those keys are omitted. The earlier 30.2 m height had no cited source and is now 30.4 m. An undated Facebook post by Steven Ward Smith calls the tower 99'9" and names an Aeromotor MC-39 model; not cited because it is social media and undated. The 'standing' status rests on the 2018 register entry; no dated source confirms it today.
